newsitem.title: UK: Licht forecasts slight fall in E.European beet area.
newsitem.headline: Licht forecasts slight fall in E.European beet area.

text.p: Eastern Europe's sugar beet sowing area should fall to 3.47 million hectares in 1997/98 from 3.57 million the previous season, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Thursday.
Area declines were expected in both Ukraine and Poland, the region's first and third largest sugar producers, while the second largest -- Russia -- would see a slight rise in area, it said.

"Leaving aside official figures, a slight rise in area is expected in the Russian Federation this year, but this will be more than counterbalanced by a drop in the Ukraine," Licht said in its first estimate of European beet areas.

The Ukrainian area was forecast at 1.35 million hectares, down from the 1.42 million sown in 1996/97. Poland was expected to sow 71,000 hectares less this season with the total area pegged at 380,000 hectares.

"A surplus of sugar was produced in Poland in 1996/97 and part of this will either have to be exported at a loss or brought forward to the current year. Consequently sowings are expected to fall this year," Licht said.
In Russia, beet sowings were forecast over an area of 1.08 million hectares, slightly higher than the 1996/97 figures of 1.07 million.
Elsewhere in the region, Hungary's sugar production surplus from its 1996/97 crop would encourage a drop in the 1997/98 sowing area.
But although more sugar was produced in the Czech Republic last year than was required for domestic needs, Licht said it was thought likely that the area would be slightly increased this year.
Hungary's beet area was forecast at 102,000 hectares after a previous 115,000, while the Czech Republic was expected to sow just 1,000 hectares more with a total area of 95,000 hectares.
